## Upstream changes 6.69.1 -> 6.70.0

**Verdict:** NEEDS ATTENTION — one real breaking change affects a specific resource's import ID format; everything else is additive.

### Breaking changes
- `resource/aws_route53domains_delegation_signer_record`: "Change the format of the import ID from `domain_name,dnssec_key_id` to `domain_name,flags,algorithm,public_key`." Any state import workflows or documentation referencing the old ID format for this resource will break. This only matters if the template's Terraform configuration or runbooks use `aws_route53domains_delegation_signer_record` imports; otherwise it has no effect.

### Variables
- none — no provider variables, environment variables, or .env entries are touched by this release. The `.env.example` is empty and the compose/providers file pins the provider version string itself (`version = "~> 6.69.1"` in `01-providers.tf`), which is the one line a host upgrading needs to bump to allow `6.70.0`.

### Data and dependencies
- none introduced by this range. No companion service (database, cache, search engine) version requirement appears anywhere in these notes.
- Note for completeness, already true before this upgrade and not a change here: the provider's required_version constraint for Terraform itself (`required_version = ">= 1.9.2, < 2.0.0"`) is set in the template file, unrelated to this provider bump.

### Before applying
- Update the version constraint in `01-providers.tf` from `~> 6.69.1` to allow `6.70.0` (e.g. `~> 6.70.0` or a suitable range), then run `terraform init -upgrade`.
- If the configuration or any external automation imports `aws_route53domains_delegation_signer_record` resources, update those import commands/scripts to the new four-field ID format (`domain_name,flags,algorithm,public_key`) before re-running imports.
- Run `terraform plan` after the upgrade and inspect diffs for any `aws_route53domains_delegation_signer_record`, `aws_guardduty_detector_feature`/`aws_guardduty_member_detector_feature`/`aws_guardduty_organization_configuration_feature` (perpetual-diff/forced-replacement bug fixes landed here — plans may show one-time corrective diffs), and `aws_prometheus_scraper` resources, since this release changes the diff/update behavior for all of them.

### Notes read
- Release notes for `v6.70.0` (2026-10-21) and the baseline `v6.69.1` (2026-10-15), both from `hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws`, plus the corresponding CHANGELOG.md entries covering the same range. The image registry comparison could not be performed (401 Unauthorized fetching image configs), so the "what the images themselves differ in" section carries no evidence and the verdict rests on the notes alone.

## Upstream changes 5.0.0 -> 5.0.1

**Verdict:** NEEDS ATTENTION — the registry diff adds a new env var, `STEAMAPPVERSION`, that the compose file and .env.example neither set nor document, and the release notes' "add support for selecting game version" feature (PR #221) depends on it.

### Breaking changes
- none found in the notes. Both listed changes are additive/internal: `feat: add support for selecting game version` (#221) and `Only clear steamapps before the last steamcmd retry` (#223).

### Variables
- `STEAMAPPVERSION` — new in the image (per WHAT THE IMAGES THEMSELVES DIFFER IN: "env `STEAMAPPVERSION` added, default 'public'"). This is not mentioned anywhere in the release notes text, but it is the mechanism behind #221 ("add support for selecting game version"). The compose file does not pass it through and .env.example does not document it. Default `public` preserves current behaviour (tracks the normal live branch), so nothing breaks by leaving it unset — but the operator has no way to pin or select a game version through this template until the compose file is updated to forward it.

### Data and dependencies
- none. No companion service (database, cache, search engine) is named in these notes, so the compose file's lack of such a pin is not a verdict-blocking mismatch here.
- #223 changes SteamCMD retry behaviour internally (steamapps is no longer cleared before every retry, only the last one) — reduces redundant re-downloads on transient failures. No action needed; this is an internal install-script fix.

### Before applying
- No backup or migration step is required for this range.
- Decide whether to expose `STEAMAPPVERSION` through the compose file (add it to the `environment:` block, e.g. `STEAMAPPVERSION: ${CS2_CLASSIC_SERVER_GAME_VERSION:-public}`) and document it in `.env.example` if pinning a specific CS2 game version is ever wanted. Not required for this upgrade to apply safely, but the capability is silently present in the image and invisible in the template otherwise.
- Confirm the image pin in `cs2-classic-server-docker-compose.yml` is bumped from `5.0.0@sha256:...` to the 5.0.1 digest (and `CS2_CLASSIC_SERVER_IMAGE_VERSION` in `.env`, if set, updated to match).

### Notes read
- v5.0.1 (2026-10-24) and v5.0.0 (2026-09-20, baseline) release notes from joedwards32/CS2, as supplied above.

**Verdict:** SAFE TO APPLY — a patch release with bug fixes and dependency bumps, no breaking changes in the notes, and the image config itself is unchanged in every field that matters.

- none found in the notes

### Variables
- none — no renamed, removed or newly required variables in this range

- none. The notes mention only internal dependency bumps (base image to 2026.10.1, Python to 3.14.8, uv, frontend to 20260930.5, various integration libraries) — none of these are companion services the compose file pins, so they don't affect the verdict.
- "WHAT THE IMAGES THEMSELVES DIFFER IN" confirms `User`, `Entrypoint`, `Cmd`, `WorkingDir`, `ExposedPorts`, `Volumes`, `Healthcheck`, and environment are identical between 2026.10.2 and 2026.10.3, so the compose file's healthcheck (`curl -f http://localhost:8123/`) and volume mounts remain valid as-is.

## Upstream changes 6.1.4 -> 6.2.0

**Verdict:** NEEDS ATTENTION — a normal minor upgrade with no documented breaking change, but one item (MariaDB note below) and the general advice to read the migration guide before applying to a production site.

### Breaking changes
- none found in the notes. No entry in the 6.2.0 (or intervening rc/beta) notes is marked as breaking; the only explicit warning concerns multi-version jumps: "Don't update directly from a version lower than 5.4, it is important that you first update to 5.4 and then update to 6.x" — not applicable here since the template is already on 6.1.4.
- A migration guide is called out specifically for this range: "⬆️ [Migration guide](https://manual.joomla.org/migrations/61-62/)" — the notes themselves give no detail on its contents, so it should be read by hand before applying to a site with non-trivial customisation (third-party extensions, template overrides).
- `"[6.2] Revert #48030 Article Preview"` — a feature (secure article preview) was added and then reverted within the same cycle, so the shipped 6.2.0 behaves as before on this point; mentioned only because it shows churn in this area, not because it is a residual change.

### Variables
- none. The compose file's `JOOMLA_*` environment block is unaffected; no variable renames, removals, or new requirements appear in the notes or in the registry diff.

### Data and dependencies
- `"[6.2] Make MariaDB a first class system"` — MariaDB support status changed in this release, but the compose file pins **PostgreSQL** (`postgres:16`), not MySQL/MariaDB, so this item does not apply to this deployment.
- `"[6.2] Lift MySQL max version in tests to version 9"` — again a MySQL-side test matrix change; irrelevant to this template's Postgres backend.
- The registry diff confirms only the Joomla version/checksum bump:
  - `env JOOMLA_VERSION: '6.1.4' -> '6.2.0'`
  - `env JOOMLA_SHA512` updated accordingly.
  No other image-level difference (user, entrypoint, command, ports, volumes, healthcheck) is reported, so none of those change in this upgrade.
- No companion-service version requirement is named by the 6.2.0 notes, so the no-SAFE-without-a-pin rule does not trigger here.

### Before applying
- Take the routine backup before any version bump (the template's own `backups` service and `joomla-data` / `joomla-postgres` volumes cover this — confirm a recent successful backup exists).
- Read the [6.1→6.2 migration guide](https://manual.joomla.org/migrations/61-62/) referenced in the release notes before applying, since it is called out specifically and its content is not included in the notes provided.
- Update the compose file's pinned digest/tag for `joomla` in the `x-images` block (and `JOOMLA_IMAGE_VERSION` in `.env` if overridden) from `6.1.4` to `6.2.0`, matching the registry's confirmed new `JOOMLA_VERSION`/`JOOMLA_SHA512`.
- No manual database migration command is mentioned in the notes; Joomla's own installer runs schema updates on first load after the upgrade, as it does for any point release.

### Notes read
- 6.2.0 (2026-10-13), 6.2.0-rc2, 6.2.0-rc1, 6.2.0-beta3 (referenced via changelog links, not separately detailed) — covering the full 6.1.4 → 6.2.0 range.
- 5.4.10 and 5.4.10-rc1 notes were present in the supplied text but describe the 5.4.x line, not the 6.1→6.2 path this template follows; not used for the verdict.
- 6.1.4 (2026-09-29) read as the baseline ("THE RELEASE THE TEMPLATE RUNS NOW") only, per instructions — its contents establish what was already true, not what changes in this move.
